items.title: 68514_Horace Henderson oral history interview
items.q: I made some things for him... I just was freelancing. I made these things, and he liked them

ctx.x: That's good. You also have here Ralph Marterie.

Ralph Marterie, quite a trumpet player. You know, that guy was real funny. When I say funny, he was comical to me, you know. He was a little busybody, you know, but he knew what he wanted, you know, and he had a swinging band, man. And I made some things for him. I didn't do too much for Ralph. I think I made about, oh, four, six numbers, you know. And I wasn't contracted to him. I just was freelancing. I made these things, and he liked them, you know, and he had a great personnel, and some swing things -- oh,…
it was quite an experience to write for that band.

items.title: 68514_Horace Henderson oral history interview
items.q: Then Ralph Marteri and his trumpet, and another guy that just passed recently, Ben Pollock. He had a nightclub in Palm Springs for quite some time. I read about this.

ctx.x: Tiny Hill lived here in Denver for some time or at Fort Lupton.
Yes, Fort Lupton, Colorado, yes, he did. He farmed 100 acres and so forth, and he had a 24 hour radio station. But we'll get back to that, though.
